summary: Round 5. The delta is verified by hash, not taken on the author's word: `git diff --cached -- . ':(exclude)baselines/review.txt' | sha256sum` = 28ac1467c7f92f121c8018ab50518d3f448c7f6093eaa996e9408655bf561aaf, byte-identical to the tree my round-3 verdict is bound to and to the non-review.txt half of round 4 (f0ac700d5198); the full staged diff is now b288318dc038 and `git diff --cached -- baselines/review.txt` shows one line rewritten and nothing else. NO TEST BYTE AND NO PRODUCTION BYTE HAS MOVED ACROSS THREE ROUNDS, so every round-3 measurement carries and I did not re-run the mutations -- re-measuring identical bytes and presenting the result as fresh is the claim non-negotiable 4 forbids. The seven new @Test methods, the three inverted assertions (two presence-to-exact-`Seal`, one equality-for-equality, each killed by a mutation), and the four round-2 pins each stand where round 3 measured them. ASKED TO CONFIRM THE COMMIT BODY'S SWEEP SENTENCE IS THE HONEST FORM OF WHAT I MEASURED: it is. The body now reads 'NO UNIQUE KILL WAS FOUND FOR THE SWEEP over the mutations review enumerated' and says plainly that the earlier 'uniquely kills no mutant' asserted a proof nobody performed. That is my round-4 wording and it is exactly what the measurement supports -- a search over an enumerated set (loop start `epoch - 1` -> `epoch - 2`; `break` after the first crossed epoch; dropping `prevEpoch = crossed`; `landed.sequence() > 1`) that came up empty, not a proof of non-existence. The adjacent claims re-check: 'four of those mutations are caught by the unit tests and NOT by it' is exact, '0.645s' is exact, and the sweep's own javadoc at CommitProtocolSimulationTest.java:209-229 still claims only measured regression evidence. I overstate nothing by confirming it. ONE MAJOR, AND IT IS IN THE ONE LINE THAT MOVED, not in a test: the rewritten `rounds:M4.47` entry replaces a false clause with another one. 'ONLY ROUND 1 WAS CHANGES-REQUESTED' was true when round 4's reviewer wrote it as the remedy, and round 4's own verdict -- `changes-requested`, one major, recorded at f0ac700d...reviewer.json -- falsified it before the fix was staged. The sentence names `.harness/review` as its witness in the same breath, and that witness answers two, not one.

findings.finding: "⚠️ ONLY ROUND 1 WAS CHANGES-REQUESTED" is false against `.harness/review`, which the same sentence cites as the record. Two M4.47 verdicts carry `changes-requested`: round 1 (e60bf990..., reviewer, one blocking plus three minors) and round 4 (f0ac700d..., reviewer, one major -- finding M4.47-R4a on this very line). The clause is a faithful copy of round 4's own remedy text ("ONLY ROUND 1 PRODUCED A CHANGES-REQUESTED VERDICT"), which was true at the moment it was written and was falsified by the verdict that carried it: round 4's reviewer was authoring a changes-requested verdict while asserting only one existed. The entry's later sentence, "Round 4 reviewed this line and found the sentence above false", discloses that round 4 found a defect but never says round 4 returned changes-requested, so nothing downstream corrects the headline. The direction of the error is AGAINST the author's interest -- it understates the justification for going past the cap -- which is why it is major and not blocking, but the file is append-only and a false clause here ships permanently, which is the same shape as M4.13f's round-3 finding about `backlog-done.md` never being rewritten. Remedy is one clause and no code or test change: "ROUNDS 1 AND 4 WERE CHANGES-REQUESTED -- round 1 on a blocking production defect, round 4 on this line alone; rounds 2 and 3 pass from both roles, minors only." That form is stable under its own recursion: it describes verdicts that already exist when it is written, and leaves round 5 free to pass.
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is append-only and is the artifact consulted when someone asks whether this project's round budget is respected or gamed. An auditor reads the M4.47 entry, runs the check the entry itself invites -- grep the M4.47 verdicts in `.harness/review` for `changes-requested` -- and gets two where the entry says one. The entry is then indistinguishable from an author trimming the record, in the exact file whose only purpose is to be honest about round counts, and the discrepancy is discovered by the first person who checks rather than by the author. Worse, it is the SECOND consecutive round in which this line asserted something the harness record contradicts (round 4 found "EVERY ROUND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN CODE, none in prose" false in both halves), so an auditor comparing the two drafts sees a correction that reintroduced the defect class it was correcting -- which is the recurring failure `backlog-done.md:115` records for M4.0 and this file records twice more. The tests and production code are untouched and unaffected; nothing runtime is wrong.
